records.text: The primary driver module tracks the Polestar ID user who is a car’s primary driver; each car can have only one primary driver. It receives order events from Polestar’s Order Management System (POMS) and records the Polestar ID in the event’s “Driver” field when both the Polestar ID and VIN are valid. A Polestar ID is valid if it exists in the Polestar ID service, verifiable by API call; a VIN is valid if it exists in Volvo’s Vehicle Internet Sale & Traceability Application (VISTA), the factory order system.

The primary driver service stores received events in an event store for replay and lets other systems update a car’s primary driver through APIs. It offers an M2M-authenticated API and a Polestar ID OAuth-authenticated API. With the Polestar ID-authenticated API, a user can edit the car’s primary driver only if the user has access to the logged-in primary driver’s credentials.

For primary driver changes, the service records the updating system, registration timestamp, and event ID; it also records the user ID for Polestar ID-authenticated API changes, the client ID for M2M-authenticated changes, and the event-emission timestamp when the change comes from an event. For POMS-event registrations, it stores the order ID. A POMS update can overwrite an API update only if the POMS order ID is new.
records.topic: primary driver change metadata and update precedence

records.text: The primary driver service maintains driver history: when a new primary driver is registered, the previous primary driver receives an end timestamp. Its APIs can also remove a primary driver from a car without registering a replacement.

On 2023-03-09, the user discussed a DynamoDB table named PrimaryDrivers for tracking a car’s primary-driver registrations and changes. The proposed schema uses VIN (string) as the partition key and Timestamp (string) as the sort key. Attributes are PolestarID, System, ChangeSource, UserID, ClientID, EventID, EventTimestamp, OrderID, PreviousOrderIDs, and EndTimestamp. System identifies the system initiating a change; ChangeSource distinguishes Event from API; UserID and ClientID identify the API caller where applicable; event and order fields record POMS event details; EndTimestamp records when a driver was removed.

The user noted that a car may have multiple previous OrderIDs if it is sold multiple times. The proposed handling was to store these in a PreviousOrderIDs list, allowing the service to check whether an incoming POMS event’s OrderID is new rather than already associated with that car’s prior ownership history.

The user specified that for an API-made change, the system creating the change must submit a system name. The name must be valid and match the ClientID, and it is stored in the DynamoDB System attribute. Example system names given by the user were “Change of Ownership” and “Polestar app.”
